main_text.p: discordiam civilem delapsa, atque hujus occasione armis Taulantiorum petita non parvam rerum suarum ac virium jacturam fecit. Demum plebs in primores ira incensa civitate eos expulit. Expulsi ad Taulantios vicinos se contulerunt, & eorum ope atque armis Epidamnum terra marique infestarunt.

Epidamnii, qui in urbe manserant, in angustias redacti Corcyraeos conditores & patronos suos missis legatis supplices rogarunt, ut autoritate sua exules ipsis reconciliare, & Taulantios ad arma ponenda inducere vellent. Sed rejecti ab iis, sive quod causam supplicum improbarent, seu quod aliud tum animo versarent, ex monito oraculi Delphensis ad[illegible, ~3 letters] Corinthios ivere, & illis coloniam dederunt. Corinthii diversis causis mo-ti, imo occasione gavisi, auxilia promiserunt.[illegible, ~2 letters] Praecipua causarum erat, quod Corcyraeis irascerentur, qui fortuna insolescerent, nec eum honorem, quem coloni debebant metropoli, exhiberent. Et jam istuc fortunae Corcyraei pervenerant, ut pecunia & classibus plus posse quam Corinthii putarentur. page.notes: The right margin carries very small, faint fragments beside "ad" and "de", too small to read; they are shown as illegible. The left edge shows show-through from the reverse page and is not transcribed. Handwritten marks at the lower right are not printed text and are left out. Exact spellings of some words in the bottom-right catchword area are uncertain. The reading "insolescerent" and "Taulantios" follow the printed forms as best seen. The catchword is read as "diuim" and marked uncertain.
